description:
FILED s473t2 (Opus triage of the 152 causeless blessed sweep rows), on main 0d783d24.
Probe scratch/s473t2/probes/p10-glob-io.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT: perl-tests/ref.t 92 (blessed number; 95 in the current run --
"IO refs are blessed into IO::File") and perl-tests/postfixderef.t 69 ("IO slot
of the temporary glob is set correctly") = 2 rows.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    my $ref = *STDOUT{IO};
    print "A: refref=[", ref($ref), "] str=[$ref]";
    print "B: slot=[", (eval '$ref->*{IO}') // 'UNDEF', "]";
    open my $fh, '<', '/etc/hostname'; my $io = *$fh{IO};
    print "C: blessed=[", (ref($io)||'-'), "]";
  perl: A: refref=[IO::File] str=[IO::File=IO(0x...)]  B: slot=[IO::File=IO(0x...)]  C: blessed=[IO::File]
  PCL : A: refref=[]         str=[GLOB(0x1)]           B: slot=[UNDEF]              C: blessed=[-]

So `*FH{IO}` answers the glob itself.  Two consequences the rows read: `ref` is
not 'IO::File', and a round trip back through `->*{IO}` (or `*{$ref}{IO}`) finds
no IO slot at all, because the value is not an IO thing.  ref.t 93 (the
`IO::File=IO(0x...)` stringification) is registered non-support today; this task
is the ref()/slot half, which is a value, not a message.
subject: BUG: `*FH{IO}` yields the GLOB, not an IO handle object -- `ref *STDOUT{IO}` is '' where perl says IO::File, and `$ref->*{IO}` is undef (perl-tests/ref.t 92/95 + postfixderef.t 69)
